newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stock index ends below 1,000 on forced sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stock index ends below 1,000 on forced sales.

text.p: Thai stocks closed below the key 1,000-point level and at their lowest since September 30, 1993, on Monday amid forced selling by brokerages of stocks held by those unable to top up margin loans, brokers said.
The index fell sharply late in the session after about 10 finance stocks hit the 10 percent limit lows followed by propery, energy and building issues, brokers said.
The index finished down 2.10 percent or 21.19 point down at 986.32. On September 30, 1993, the index closed at 971.44.
"Forced selling was behind the fall today," said Sanpong Limthanrongkul of Jardine Fleming Thanakom Securities.
Among major finance firms whose prices hit limit down were CMIC Finance and Securities, General Finance and Securities and Siam City Credit Finance and Securities.
Brokers said a private sector rescue fund, which entered the market on Friday to shore up the battered market was used again today by banks and brokers to uplift prices.

But they did not know how much was spent, although brokers speculated about 1.0 billion baht was disbursed on Friday from the 15.7 billion baht. "Foreigners continued to sell today because they did not have confidence in Thai politics and economics," said Sanpong.
On Friday, total net sales by foreigners amounted to 1.7 billion baht, brokers said.
Foreigners were now more pessimistic about Thai politics and economy after Moody's earlier last week downgraded Thailand's short-term debt ratings.
Thai Farmers Bank fell two baht to 163. General Finance and Securities dropped 5.50 to 53 and Nava Finance was down 4.75 baht to 45.25.
Support is seen by some brokers at 980-point on Tuesday with resistance at 1,000, brokers said. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 252-9950
